texts.text: A long way down. She said the idol is at the bottom. You believed her.
The mouth of it. Land a fall of forty metres and you will not get up. Shorter falls still break you. Let the rope out.
Five of them, around a fire that went out a long time ago.
The rock ends. Beyond the lip there is no far wall you can see, and no floor. It goes down further than the light does.
Small ledges, far between. Let the rope out slowly.
Flat ground. It feels wrong after so much rope. The lamps lead to the one corner where the dark opens again.
The edge. Below the corner, against the wall, there is a ledge. Everything else is air.
From here it is rope and nerve. The footholds are a full line apart.
Someone laid them here. Rows of them, standing, facing the dark. You do not look at the faces.
Small ledges, far between. Let the rope out slowly.
Flat ground. It feels wrong after so much rope. The lamps lead to the one corner where the dark opens again.
The lamps ahead are going out, one by one. Something is walking down the line toward you.
The edge. Below the corner, against the wall, there is a ledge. Everything else is air.
Small ledges, far between. Let the rope out slowly.
A bridge of fallen stone, broken in the middle. The far side is a hook's throw away.
A bell on a stone gallows, hung by the miners. Throw your hook at it. Anything hunting will come to the sound instead of to you.
Something pale is coiled out there in the dark. It does not move while you watch it.
Small ledges, far between. Let the rope out slowly.
A shelf of rock the size of a field, fallen across the rift. The only way on is over its far corner. Follow the lamps.
The edge. Below the corner, against the wall, there is a ledge. Everything else is air.
No balcony below. Only what your hook can reach.
Below you the rift is plugged, wall to wall, by one fallen slab the size of a town. There is no way through it. There are holes in the wall.
Three holes, low in the wall. One goes through. You will have to crawl.
You can stand. Your knees are bleeding. Somewhere ahead, green light.
Five of them, around a fire that went out a long time ago.
Under the Lid the rift opens wider than before, and the walls glow. Three pieces of the idol were hidden in the deep. The foundry door wants all three.
A passage behind the brackets. Something glints inside.
Flat ground. It feels wrong after so much rope. The lamps lead to the one corner where the dark opens again.
The lamps ahead are going out, one by one. Something is walking down the line toward you.
The edge. Below the corner, against the wall, there is a ledge. Everything else is air.
Four kilns, cold, each on a bracket of its own. Light them all.
Roots of something that should not be this deep. They cross the whole rift, wall to wall, thick as streets. You will have to walk them.
The root is moving under your feet. No. Something is moving along it.
The root is moving under your feet. No. Something is moving along it.
The water left. The mist stayed, and the falls still pour out of the walls into nothing. They will push you off if you let them.
Small ledges, far between. Let the rope out slowly.
Small ledges, far between. Let the rope out slowly.
Legs on stone, above you. Many. Keep going down.
Flat ground. It feels wrong after so much rope. The lamps lead to the one corner where the dark opens again.
The edge. Below the corner, against the wall, there is a ledge. Everything else is air.
From here it is rope and nerve. The footholds are a full line apart.
Four plates. Everyone stands on one. Alone, the door will not wait for you.
The galleries end. For the next two hundred metres there is only wet wall and what your hook can find on it. Do not rush it.
Legs on stone, above you. Many. Keep going down.
A whole village fell into the dark and caught on its own chains. The houses hang out there over nothing, lamps still lit. The way on is across them.
Something glints on that roof.
A shelf of rock the size of a field, fallen across the rift. The only way on is over its far corner. Follow the lamps.
The lamps ahead are going out, one by one. Something is walking down the line toward you.
The edge. Below the corner, against the wall, there is a ledge. Everything else is air.
Cold light. Crystals the size of towers have grown clean across the rift. They are slick as glass, and they slope. Once you step on, you are going where they go.
A crack in the wall, glowing from inside.
A shelf of rock the size of a field, fallen across the rift. The only way on is over its far corner. Follow the lamps.
The edge. Below the corner, against the wall, there is a ledge. Everything else is air.
Heat from below. Far down there is a lake of it, and it lights the whole rift red. The kilns on the walls still burn.
Legs on stone, above you. Many. Keep going down.
The rift is floored here, wall to wall, almost. Someone lit a line of lamps across it. It is a long way to the edge.
The lamps ahead are going out, one by one. Something is walking down the line toward you.
The edge. Below the corner, against the wall, there is a ledge. Everything else is air.
No balcony below. Only what your hook can reach.
Legs on stone, above you. Many. Keep going down.
No floor. Only thin rods of iron, a full rope apart, and the heat. You cannot stand on them. Swing, let go at the top, throw again. Rest where the iron is wide. Not every rod holds.
You made it across. Your hands will not stop shaking.
The door wears the mark of the idol. It wants all three pieces.
This is where they come from.
At the far end, on the altar, it waits. Like she said.
Light, far above. Take it home.
No ember on this road. No kiln, no light, nothing you were sent down here to find. What you skip, you skip.
Scratched into the rock, low down: THE SHORT WAY. Under it someone drew a skull. There is a ledge a running jump past the end of the balcony, and a violet light on it.
Someone left this here for whoever came the short way. Take it. Then look down: the balcony is one rope below.

Someone left this here for whoever came the short way. Take it. Then look down: the balcony is one rope below.
Ribs. Each one longer than a street, grown into the wall. Whatever it was, it died before anyone dug here. The rift was cut around it.
Barely wider than your shoulders. You go in on your hands and knees.
It narrows. Breathe out and push.
Somewhere above you is the weight of the Lid. You try not to think about it.
It ends. Someone got this far and stopped. Back out, feet first.
A pocket of bones. No way on. The hole you dropped through is above you.
